=== (3) HAZARDS / FRAGILE ASSUMPTIONS ===

HAZARD-1: parseSummaryCount scopes to the '== SUMMARY ==' block. If a future claimlint change removes or renames that block header, BOTH standing triggers fail loudly (control 6 greps for it, so the regression catches it first). If a future claimlint puts the count somewhere else, the loud failure forces a conscious repoint — that is the designed behaviour.

HAZARD-2: The C7 SUMMARY label 'C7 unabsorbed findings' is a substring of nothing else in current output, but the old detail line 'C7 UNABSORBED unabsorbed findings: N' is one renaming away from colliding. The SUMMARY-block scoping makes a collision harmless (the label only matches inside the block), but if the SUMMARY row itself ever prints 'C7 UNABSORBED unabsorbed findings N', the label match would hit the detail... no — the SUMMARY block contains only the one C7 row, so the parse stays correct as long as the count is the first digit-run after the label. Keep the label distinct from detail-section text.

HAZARD-3: The archive parser derives task IDs from findings FILENAMES (findings/<TASKID>-<slug>.json). A findings file whose name does not follow the convention (e.g. 'STANDING-ABSORB-absorption.json' — no T-prefix) cannot be attributed to a task and will not refuse archiving. The findings JSON's internal task_id field is authoritative but not read (would need per-file JSON parsing; the filename convention is documented in findings/README.md).

HAZARD-4: The C3 growth control (control 9) depends on the `_standing` prior surviving between two standing runs in the same script — which works only because nothing rewrites the scratch kanban in between. This is CODE.STANDING-STATE-FRAGILE territory; if that defect is ever fixed by making _standing a first-class store key, re-check control 8/9 (they should still pass).

HAZARD-5: persistStandingState skips rewriting when '_standing' already exists in the file, so the C3 prior is only ever written by the FIRST standing run against a fresh store. The control order in the regression script (null+seeded runs first) is what sets prior=3; reordering the controls would change the asserted '(was 3)' values.

HAZARD-6: The drift-stub claimlint (control 7) exits 1, but std.process.run captures stdout regardless of exit code — the loud failure fires on MISSING MARKERS, not on claimlint's exit code. claimlint exits 1 on real failures (C7>0 etc.) while printing a full summary; that is the normal operating case and must keep working (it does: seeded control 3 passes with claimlint exiting 1).

WEAK-1: The resume surface parser (runClaimlintSummary, token-position based) still works against current output (verified: C1a/C1b/C2/C6 positions unchanged by T356's bracket-appended names) but is NOT part of this row's regression coverage. If a future rename shifts those token positions, resume's gate block degrades to '?' — visible, not silent, but untested.

WEAK-2: The archive absorption check's loud warnings go to stderr; `managent archive` in the fleet runs without asserting on them. The REFUSAL itself (the count in the 'refused: ... unabsorbed findings' line) is the real gate; the warning is for humans.
